doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: Banjo, mandolin and the Italian Intermezzo session
summary: Pallo plays banjo for Dixieland and mandolin for sessions, including a one-day CD with Bucky and Ken Peplowski's charts.

story.theme_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section: instruments and players
story.community_name: Banjo, guitar and the rhythm section's changing role

blocks.x: Do you get calls to play what I guess we’d call traditional jazz or Dixieland?
And that’s pretty simple, I might have to bring the banjo out on that.
Oh you’re a banjoist too when you need to be.

Yes. Not a great banjo player but enough to get by on the banjo, and the mandolin, I’ve been on calls for sessions on mandolin which I have to woodshed at least two weeks before the session because it’s E A D G, it’s like a violin tuning. And I have to go all through that again and I have to start getting my act together on the mandolin. The last session I had was with Bucky, we did an Italian Intermezzo it was called, and we had that
one day and we did a whole CD in one day, and oh I can’t think — he plays clarinet, he wrote the charts.

Yes. Ken Peplowski wrote the charts. And that was pretty tough because it was all written out. And to play the mandolin, now I’m more with the guitar, and someone said, from California, they said why don’t you do what they did out in California like behind Dean Martin and all those recordings, a lot of them used guitar tuning. But I said oh jeez I don’t want to do that because then it might not sound right. So I kept the mandolin tuning. That’s why Bucky always recommends me, because the tuning is a little more high pitched and more like mandolin. But it’s tough. I really don’t want to do too much of that. It’s a lot of work. I had to woodshed for two weeks at least.
Well it’s tiny too, isn’t it?

It’s very tiny. But it’s easy to get around. Very easy to get around. And I’ve tried violin since I play mandolin, and I just can’t play violin. It’s the same tuning but it’s the right hand, very important, the bow.
